title: Matching a Value
goal: Compare a value against options, and get a value back.

sections.text: `match` compares one value against a list of options. You will recognise the shape from `switch` in C, Java, or JavaScript, but three things are different.

sections.caption: Each arm is a value, an arrow, and what to do.

sections.text: First, there is no fall-through. The first arm that matches runs, and nothing after it. You never write `break`.
Second, a `match` must cover every possible value. The compiler checks this and refuses to build otherwise. `_` is the catch-all arm that handles everything you did not list.
Third, `match` is an expression, so it can produce a value straight into a `let`. Every arm must then produce the same type.

sections.caption: No semicolons after the arms, and one after the closing brace.

sections.text: This deck only matches on plain values like numbers and booleans. Matching on enums and pulling their data apart is a larger topic called pattern matching, and it has a deck of its own later.

explanation: Compare a value against options, and get a value back.
